risk_classes.label_it: Modello di IA per finalità generali

classification_decision_tree.question: Is it an 'AI system' (Art. 3(1)) or a GPAI model (Art. 3(63)) within the scope of Art. 2, and no exclusion of Art. 2 applies?
Does the use fall under any prohibited practice of Art. 5?

Is the system a safety component of a product, or itself a product, covered by Annex I legislation AND subject to third-party conformity assessment under that legislation? (See Art. 6(1a)-(1c), inserted in 2026: components used only for non-safety aspects are not safety components.)
Is the system used in one of the areas and use cases listed in Annex III?

Does a derogation of Art. 6(3) apply (narrow procedural task, improving a completed human activity, detecting decision patterns, preparatory task) AND the system does NOT perform profiling of natural persons?
classification_decision_tree.yes: not high-risk — document the assessment (Art. 6(4)) and register (Art. 49(2)); continue at step 6

classification_decision_tree.question: Does the system interact with natural persons, generate synthetic content, perform emotion recognition / biometric categorisation, or produce deep fakes?
Independently of steps 2–6: is the organisation the provider of a GPAI model? If yes, does it meet the systemic-risk criteria of Art. 51?

hitl_gate: The final class is always confirmed by a human (HITL) and recorded in the audit log with the rationale.

role_change_rule.note: A distributor, importer, deployer or other third party becomes a provider when it rebrands, substantially modifies, or changes the intended purpose of a high-risk system.

entries.what: Chapters I and II apply (unchanged), except the new prohibitions below
Entry into force of Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (third day after publication on 24.7.2026); Articles 102 to 110 apply
General date of application, incl. Art. 50 transparency obligations (unchanged)
New prohibitions of Art. 5(1)(ba) and (bb) with Art. 5(1a) and (1b) apply; providers of generative AI systems placed on the market before 2 Aug 2026 must comply with Art. 50(2)
National AI regulatory sandboxes operational; Commission delegated acts under Art. 2(13) due
Commission guidance and template for the post-market monitoring plan due
Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply to high-risk AI systems under Art. 6(2) and Annex III
Notified bodies under Annex I Section A legislation must apply for designation
Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply to high-risk AI systems under Art. 6(1) and Annex I
High-risk AI systems intended for public authorities placed on the market before application must comply

key_changes.change: AI literacy: providers and deployers 'shall take measures to support the development of AI literacy'; no duty to guarantee a specific level for any individual

New article on processing special categories of personal data for bias detection and correction; replaces Art. 10(5), which is deleted, and extends the possibility to other AI systems and to deployers under the same safeguards
New prohibited practices (ba) non-consensual intimate or sexually explicit content of identifiable persons and (bb) child sexual abuse material, with conditions in (1a) and (1b)
New paragraphs 1a-1c narrowing what counts as a safety component and as third-party conformity assessment
Simplified technical documentation form extended to small mid-caps (SMCs)
Initial provider must cooperate with the new provider; written agreement in 25(4) now also covers AI models
FRIA may cross-reference or include the relevant parts of the DPIA; AI Office template to allow this
AI Office exclusively competent for AI systems based on a GPAI model of the same provider and for systems integrated in very large online platforms or search engines, with listed exceptions
SMEs' and SMCs' interests to be taken into account; for SMCs each fine is capped at the lower of the percentage or the amount; breaches of Art. 25(2) and (4) added to Art. 99(4)

penalties_original_art_99.verification: primary source read (Art. 99 and its amendment by 2026/1744 Art. 1(38)): amounts unchanged; for SMEs and SMCs each fine is the lower of the percentage or the amount (Art. 99(6) and new 6a)
